mcq.q: Which word has the long sound /uː/?
mcq.explanation: Food has /uː/. The others have /ʊ/.

mcq.q: Which word has the short sound /ʊ/?
mcq.explanation: Cook has /ʊ/.

mcq.q: Which word has the sound /æ/?
mcq.explanation: Apple has /æ/.

mcq.q: Which is a minimal pair for /f/ and /v/?
mcq.explanation: They differ in the last sound.

mcq.q: A balanced diet is a diet that
options: has the right amounts of all types of food
mcq.explanation: It has energy, body-building and protective foods and water.

mcq.q: Which foods mainly give us energy?
mcq.explanation: They are carbohydrates.

mcq.q: Which foods help the body to grow?
mcq.explanation: They contain protein.

mcq.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: I would like be a nurse.
I would like to being a nurse.
I would like to be a nurse.
I would likes to be a nurse.
mcq.explanation: The pattern is would like to be + noun phrase.

mcq.q: 'She would like to be ___.' Which fits?
mcq.explanation: A noun phrase follows be.

mcq.q: What is a good habit for a listener?
options: Look at the speaker and do not interrupt
mcq.explanation: Good listeners give attention.

mcq.q: The short form of 'I would' is
mcq.explanation: I would can be shortened to I'd.

mcq.q: What does 'thin' mean?
options: With little flesh on the body
mcq.explanation: Thin is the opposite of plump.

mcq.q: Independent reading means
options: reading aloud to the class only
reading on your own without being told what to read
mcq.explanation: You choose and read for yourself.

mcq.q: In the five-finger test, four or five fingers on a page mean the book is
mcq.explanation: Many unknown words show that it is too hard.

mcq.q: Which is an example of extensive reading?
options: Reading one line for a test
Reading many story books in your free time
Learning a poem for an exam
mcq.explanation: Extensive reading means reading widely.

mcq.q: What is fluency?
mcq.explanation: Fluent readers read smoothly.

mcq.q: Which is a way of choosing a book?
options: Choose a book with no words
Read the title, cover and first page
mcq.explanation: These clues show whether the book interests you.

mcq.q: A reading log helps you to
mcq.explanation: It records titles, dates and what you liked.

mcq.q: When reading silently, you should
mcq.explanation: Silent reading helps you focus.

mcq.q: Which is a good rule for a reading club?
options: Take books home and keep them
mcq.explanation: Politeness keeps everyone included.

mcq.q: Which material gives you news?
mcq.explanation: Newspapers report news.

mcq.q: You meet a new word while reading alone. What can you do?
options: Use clues in the sentence and check a dictionary later
mcq.explanation: Context and a dictionary help.

mcq.q: Why should you return borrowed books on time?
options: So others can read them too
mcq.explanation: It shows responsibility and fairness.

mcq.q: Which is a sentence starter for sharing a story?
mcq.explanation: It helps you tell what you liked.

mcq.q: An adjective is a word that
mcq.explanation: Adjectives describe nouns.

mcq.q: What is the comparative form of 'tall'?
mcq.explanation: Short adjectives add er.

mcq.q: What is the superlative form of 'big'?
mcq.explanation: The last letter doubles: big, bigger, biggest.

mcq.q: What is the comparative of 'happy'?
mcq.explanation: Change y to i and add er.

mcq.q: What is the superlative of 'good'?
mcq.explanation: Good, better, best.

mcq.q: What is the comparative of 'bad'?
mcq.explanation: Bad, worse, worst.

mcq.q: Which is correct?
options: This is more beautiful than that.
This is more beautifuler than that.
mcq.explanation: Long adjectives use more.

mcq.q: Which phrase has adjectives in the correct order?
mcq.explanation: The order is size, shape, colour.

mcq.q: Which is correct?
options: Kevin is more taller than Musa.
mcq.explanation: Use the er form with than.

mcq.q: Choose the sentence with a superlative.
options: Chege is very tall than Ben.
mcq.explanation: The tallest points to the top of three or more.

mcq.q: Which word is the opposite of plump?
mcq.explanation: Plump means fat in a pleasant way and thin is its opposite.

mcq.q: Which is the comparative form of 'little' (amount)?
mcq.explanation: Little, less, least.

mcq.q: A narrative is
options: a story that tells what happened
mcq.explanation: It tells events in order.

mcq.q: Which part of a narrative tells how it finished?
mcq.explanation: The ending gives the result.

mcq.q: Which sentence has a simile?
options: The bread was as soft as a pillow.
mcq.explanation: It compares bread with a pillow using as ... as.

mcq.q: Which word helps to show order in a narrative?
mcq.explanation: Time words show order.

mcq.q: About how long is a Grade 4 narrative composition?
mcq.explanation: The design asks for about 60 to 80 words.

mcq.q: Why is it important to plan a composition?
options: It keeps the ideas in order
It makes the story longer without ideas
mcq.explanation: A plan shows what comes first, next and last.

mcq.q: Which is the correct order for the parts of a narrative?
mcq.explanation: Stories move from beginning to end.

mcq.q: Which phrase is a better word for 'nice' food?
mcq.explanation: Delicious is a stronger, more exact word.

mcq.q: A story that you heard on the radio and write in your own words is
mcq.explanation: You tell the same story in new words.

mcq.q: Which detail uses the sense of smell?
mcq.explanation: It describes something smelt.

mcq.q: In the story shape, the highest point is
mcq.explanation: Events rise to an exciting part.

mcq.q: Which sentence would be a good first sentence?
options: On Saturday, Mama took me to the supermarket.
mcq.explanation: It tells when, who and where.

short.q: Write two sentences beginning 'I would like to be' and give a reason in each.
short.answer: I would like to be a doctor because I want to help sick people. I would like to be a runner because I love sport.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct sentence with reason, and 1 for accuracy.

short.q: Name the three groups of food on a healthy plate and give one example of each.
short.answer: Energy foods such as ugali; body-building foods such as beans; protective foods such as spinach.
short.working: 1 mark for each group with an example.

short.q: State two habits of a good listener.
short.answer: Look at the speaker; do not interrupt; think about what you hear; ask a question when the speaker finishes (any two).
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain what Baraka learnt from his grandmother.
short.answer: He learnt that ugali and tea are not enough. A balanced diet with energy foods, body-building foods, fruit and vegetables and clean water keeps a person strong and healthy.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four correct points.

short.q: Write two words with the sound /uː/ and two words with /ʊ/.
short.answer: /uː/: food, spoon. /ʊ/: book, cook.
short.working: 1 mark for each correct pair.

short.q: State three materials you can read for pleasure.
short.answer: Story books, poems, magazines, comics, newspapers (any three).
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain how to use the five-finger test.
short.answer: Open a page and read. Hold up a finger for each new word. Count the fingers: few means the book is right, many means it is too hard.
short.working: 1 mark for the method, 1 mark for few, 1 mark for many.

short.q: Give two reasons why we should read widely.
short.answer: It builds vocabulary and improves reading speed and understanding. It gives knowledge and enjoyment.
short.working: 1 mark for each reason.

short.q: Describe how you would set up a reading club in your class.
short.answer: Choose a day, time and place; give members roles; agree on rules such as taking turns; and read silently then share what was read.
short.working: 1 mark for each of four points.

short.q: Read: 'Juma asked his mother to add vegetables to his lunch.' Say why Juma did this, using the story 'A Pot of Vegetables'.
short.answer: Mama Zuri told him vegetables give vitamins that protect the body from sickness, so he wanted to stay healthy.
short.working: 1 mark for vitamins or protection and 1 mark for linking to Juma.

short.q: Write the comparative and superlative of: happy, beautiful.
short.answer: happier, happiest; more beautiful, most beautiful.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Put the adjectives in the right order: a (red, round, big) balloon.
short.answer: a big round red balloon
short.working: 1 mark for size first and 1 mark for shape before colour.

short.q: Write the missing forms: good, better, ___ ; bad, ___ , worst; many, more, ___ .
short.answer: best; worse; most
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Write three sentences about your family or school: one comparative, one superlative and one with two adjectives in the right order.
short.answer: My brother is taller than I am. He is the tallest boy in his class. He has a big round bag.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Explain why 'more better' is wrong. Give the correct form.
short.answer: Better is already the comparative form, so we do not add more. The correct form is better.
short.working: 1 mark for the reason and 1 mark for the correct form.

short.q: List the three parts of a narrative and say what each tells.
short.answer: Beginning: who, where and when. Middle: the events. End: how it finished.
short.working: 1 mark for each part.

short.q: Write two similes about food.
short.answer: The bread was as soft as a pillow. The juice was as sweet as honey.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Arrange in order: (a) Then she paid. (b) Grace entered the shop. (c) Finally, she went home.
short.answer: b, a, c
short.working: 1 mark for b first and 1 mark for a then c.

short.q: Give two reasons why we plan before writing a story.
short.answer: It puts ideas in order and makes sure we do not forget important events.
short.working: 1 mark for each.

short.q: Write a narrative of about 60 words about a visit to a shop. Use one simile and two time words.
short.answer: A story of about 60 words with beginning, middle and end, one simile, two time words such as first and then, and correct punctuation.
short.working: 1 mark each for beginning, events, simile, time words, and punctuation.
